isocountry

isocountry provides ISO country, currency, and market identifier codes as plain data frames, with no dependencies.

Datasets

  • isocountry: ISO 3166-1 country codes with UN M49 regions and membership in the OECD, the European Union (EU), the euro area (EMU), and the European Economic Area (EEA).
  • isocurrency: ISO 4217 currency codes with minor units and the countries using each currency.
  • isocurrency_historic: withdrawn ISO 4217 currency codes, e.g. the national currencies replaced by the euro.
  • isomic: ISO 10383 market identifier codes (MICs) for exchanges and other trading venues.

Across the datasets, country_code is the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (alpha_2 in isocountry) and country_number is the numeric code, so the datasets join easily. Use tibble::as_tibble() or data.table::as.data.table() if you prefer tibbles or data.tables.

Installation

You can install the released version of isocountry from CRAN with:

install.packages("isocountry")

And the development version from GitHub with:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("m-muecke/isocountry")

Usage 

library(isocountry)

Look up a country:

subset(
  isocountry,
  alpha_2 == "DE",
  c(name, alpha_3, country_number, region_name, eu_member, emu_member)
)
#>       name alpha_3 country_number region_name eu_member emu_member
#> 84 Germany     DEU            276      Europe      TRUE       TRUE

List the euro area members:

isocountry$name[isocountry$emu_member]
#>  [1] "Austria"                     "Belgium"                    
#>  [3] "Bulgaria"                    "Croatia"                    
#>  [5] "Cyprus"                      "Estonia"                    
#>  [7] "Finland"                     "France"                     
#>  [9] "Germany"                     "Greece"                     
#> [11] "Ireland"                     "Italy"                      
#> [13] "Latvia"                      "Lithuania"                  
#> [15] "Luxembourg"                  "Malta"                      
#> [17] "Netherlands, Kingdom of the" "Portugal"                   
#> [19] "Slovakia"                    "Slovenia"                   
#> [21] "Spain"

Find the countries using a currency:

subset(isocurrency, currency_code == "CHF", c(country_name, country_code))
#>      country_name country_code
#> 135 Liechtenstein           LI
#> 223   Switzerland           CH

Look up exchanges by their MIC:

subset(isomic, mic %in% c("XNYS", "XLON", "XETR"), c(mic, market_name, country_code))
#>       mic                   market_name country_code
#> 2433 XETR                         XETRA           DE
#> 2577 XLON         LONDON STOCK EXCHANGE           GB
#> 2673 XNYS NEW YORK STOCK EXCHANGE, INC.           US

Add the currencies to the countries:

countries <- merge(
  isocountry[c("alpha_2", "name", "region_name")],
  isocurrency[c("country_code", "currency_code", "currency_name")],
  by.x = "alpha_2",
  by.y = "country_code"
)
head(countries)
#>   alpha_2                 name region_name currency_code         currency_name
#> 1      AD              Andorra      Europe           EUR                  Euro
#> 2      AE United Arab Emirates        Asia           AED            UAE Dirham
#> 3      AF          Afghanistan        Asia           AFN               Afghani
#> 4      AG  Antigua and Barbuda    Americas           XCD East Caribbean Dollar
#> 5      AI             Anguilla    Americas           XCD East Caribbean Dollar
#> 6      AL              Albania      Europe           ALL                   Lek

Data sources

Dataset Source
isocountry ISO 3166-1 codes and OECD and EU membership from Wikipedia, regions from the UN Statistics Division
isocurrency, isocurrency_historic ISO 4217 lists one and three, published by SIX as the ISO 4217 maintenance agency
isomic ISO 10383 list, published by the ISO 10383 registration authority

The data in the development version is refreshed monthly. The package code is MIT licensed, and the bundled data remains subject to the terms of its sources.

isocountry is inspired by the ISO-3166-Countries-with-Regional-Codes project.
